response.value: She locates a specimen of a more distantly related snake to see if it has a forked tongue
steps: To determine the ancestral state of a trait in a group of closely related species, biologists use an outgroup.
An outgroup is a more distantly related organism that serves as a reference group.
By examining the trait in a more distantly related snake (the outgroup), the biologist can infer whether the forked tongue was present in the common ancestor.
Option (B) correctly describes the use of an outgroup to determine the ancestral state.
